title: Watari-ago-niju-hozo-shikuchi
guidance: A post carries two stacked tenons: the lower one takes the 桁 girder, the upper one runs through both the girder and the 梁 beam above and is cut flush with the beam's top, and a 渡り顎 housing across the girder takes the beam's chin.  The layout follows the carpentry-school build log (hainankenchiku.jimdofree.com; diyshufu.com/job-training-of-carpenter/1754/) and the assembly GIF by @thejoinery_jp (tweet 771307153583812610).

usage: Double-tenon crossing over a post: a 桁 girder sits on the post's lower tenon, a 梁 beam crosses on it, the post's upper tenon runs through girder and beam alike and is cut flush with the beam's top, and a 渡り顎 housing in the girder takes the beam's chin at the crossing.
strengths: The lower tenon fixes the girder on the post without hollowing the post's core.
The upper tenon runs right through the girder and the beam, so the joint resists uplift and ties all three timbers in line.
The 渡り顎 housing and chin stop the beam shifting along the crossing, and the shoulders either side keep the beam's bearing full width.
weaknesses: The girder loses its housing depth (about 18 mm) across a 78 mm band, and the beam loses the same at its chin.
The through tenon and the jaw must be set out together; the carpentry-school build log records over two hours of scribing and a struggle to open the mortise right through.
